Running the planned analyses (33)…

Distribution of product_revenue: product_revenue has a median of 51.1 and mean of 61.1 (range 3.25 to 260); the distribution is right-skewed (a few very large values). Medians are a safer summary than means here. The chart is cut at the 99th percentile (59 larger values not shown); the statistics use every value.
Outliers in product_revenue: product_revenue: 199 of 5846 values (3.4%) fall outside the usual range (-50.5 to 164).

Relationships between numeric columns: Strongest relationships: returns_refund_amount_total & returns_refund_amount_avg: r=1.00; unit_price & list_price: r=0.99; unit_cost & list_price: r=0.94. Correlation shows columns move together, not that one causes the other. unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio is a ratio, so these correlations use its per-row values (not a group-level ratio of sums). Not reported because one column is calculated from the other: unit_price = unit_cost × unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio; returns_refund_amount_avg = quantity × unit_price; product_revenue = quantity × unit_price.

product_revenue by sales_channel: Average product_revenue is highest for sales_channel = Web Store (62.1) and lowest for Marketplace (59.6). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.128, eta²=0.001, negligible effect).

product_revenue by payment_method: Average product_revenue is highest for payment_method = Cash on Delivery (64.6) and lowest for Bank Transfer (57.7). The difference is statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.0296, eta²=0.002, negligible effect).

product_revenue by region: Average product_revenue is highest for region = Unknown (63.9) and lowest for West (59.4). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.723, eta²=0.001, negligible effect).

Robustness check: product_revenue by category: Robustness check for product_revenue by category using medians: highest median in Apparel (61.2), lowest in Stationery (12.9). Kruskal-Wallis p<0.001 - the group difference holds up without relying on means.
Where product_revenue comes from (category): The top 3 values of category account for 78% of total product_revenue (leader: Kitchen, 31%).

product_revenue over time: product_revenue (sum per month) shows a statistically significant upward trend (about +75% across the period, p<0.001). Best month: 2025-05-01 (22.0K); weakest: 2024-01-01 (8,034). The first and last months may be partial.

product_revenue by day of the week: product_revenue does not vary reliably by day of the week (ANOVA on period totals p=1, effect size eta²=0.003). Highest: Tue (536); lowest: Sun (485); overall 499. Values are the average daily total, not a per-row average. By month of the year, product_revenue does not vary reliably (p=1, eta²=0.093): highest May (17.2K), lowest Jan (12.1K).

returns_count by sales_channel: The '1.0' rate for returns_count is highest in sales_channel = Marketplace (8.9%) and lowest in Social Shop (8.1%); across all rows it is 8.4%. The difference is not statistically significant (chi-square p=0.606, Cramér's V=0.01, negligible effect).

product_revenue: sales_channel × region: Across sales_channel and region, product_revenue is highest for Social Shop × Unknown (75.2) and lowest for Marketplace × East (55.4), a 1.4× gap. Only combinations with at least 10 rows are shown; these cell-level gaps are not individually tested, so treat them as leads to check rather than proven differences. The chart draws only the 3 biggest sales_channel and 6 biggest region values (of 3 and 7); the best and weakest cells are found over all data.

Summary of numeric columns: Descriptive summary of 8 numeric columns (count, share missing, mean, median, standard deviation, minimum and maximum). For unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio the mean is the ratio of sums (total of the first column over total of the second), not an average of row ratios.

unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio over time: unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio (ratio of sums per month) shows a weak, non-significant downward trend (about -1% across the period, p=0.243). Best month: 2024-09-01 (2.03); weakest: 2025-09-01 (1.94). The first and last months may be partial.

unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio by sales_channel: unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio (total unit_price over total unit_cost) is highest for sales_channel = Social Shop (2) and lowest for Marketplace (1.99). The difference is not statistically significant (permutation test on the ratio of sums p=0.654, eta²=0.000, negligible effect).

unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio by sales_channel (table): unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio for each sales_channel value ranked by overall value. Groups with few rows give unstable averages, so look at the Rows column first.

unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio by payment_method: unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio (total unit_price over total unit_cost) is highest for payment_method = Unknown (2.04) and lowest for Cash on Delivery (1.97). The difference is not statistically significant (permutation test on the ratio of sums p=0.0679, eta²=0.002, negligible effect).

unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio by region: unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio (total unit_price over total unit_cost) is highest for region = Islands (2.01) and lowest for West (1.98). The difference is not statistically significant (permutation test on the ratio of sums p=0.474, eta²=0.001, negligible effect).

unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio by category: unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio (total unit_price over total unit_cost) is highest for category = Home Decor (2.12) and lowest for Garden (1.84). The difference is statistically significant (permutation test on the ratio of sums p<0.001, eta²=0.077, medium effect).

unit_price over time: unit_price (mean per month) shows a weak, non-significant downward trend (about -3% across the period, p=0.223). Best month: 2024-02-01 (40.6); weakest: 2025-06-01 (34.1). The first and last months may be partial.

unit_price by sales_channel: Average unit_price is highest for sales_channel = Web Store (36.8) and lowest for Social Shop (36.4). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.67, eta²=0.000, negligible effect).
unit_price by sales_channel (table): unit_price for each sales_channel value ranked by average. Groups with few rows give unstable averages, so look at the Rows column first.

unit_price by payment_method: Average unit_price is highest for payment_method = Cash on Delivery (37.7) and lowest for Bank Transfer (35.3). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.207, eta²=0.001, negligible effect).

unit_price by region: Average unit_price is highest for region = Unknown (38.8) and lowest for West (35.6). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.486, eta²=0.001, negligible effect).

unit_price by category: Average unit_price is highest for category = Apparel (46.1) and lowest for Stationery (9.86). The difference is statistically significant (ANOVA p<0.001, eta²=0.358, large effect).

unit_cost over time: unit_cost (mean per month) shows a weak, non-significant downward trend (about -3% across the period, p=0.344). Best month: 2024-02-01 (20.5); weakest: 2024-12-01 (17). The first and last months may be partial.

unit_cost by sales_channel: Average unit_cost is highest for sales_channel = Web Store (18.4) and lowest for Social Shop (18.2). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.76, eta²=0.000, negligible effect).
unit_cost by sales_channel (table): unit_cost for each sales_channel value ranked by average. Groups with few rows give unstable averages, so look at the Rows column first.

unit_cost by payment_method: Average unit_cost is highest for payment_method = Cash on Delivery (19.1) and lowest for Bank Transfer (17.8). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.0853, eta²=0.001, negligible effect).

unit_cost by region: Average unit_cost is highest for region = Unknown (19.7) and lowest for West (17.9). The difference is not statistically significant (ANOVA p=0.575, eta²=0.001, negligible effect).

unit_cost by category: Average unit_cost is highest for category = Kitchen (23) and lowest for Stationery (4.83). The difference is statistically significant (ANOVA p<0.001, eta²=0.321, large effect).

product_revenue by category: Average product_revenue is highest for category = Apparel (77.3) and lowest for Stationery (16.3). The difference is statistically significant (ANOVA p<0.001, eta²=0.177, large effect).

unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio by day of the week: unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio does not vary reliably by day of the week (Kruskal-Wallis p=1, effect size eta²=0.006). Highest: Sun (2.02); lowest: Tue (1.98); overall 2. Values are total unit_price over total unit_cost for each day of the week; the test compares daily ratios. By month of the year, unit_price_to_unit_cost_ratio does not vary reliably (p=1, eta²=0.433): highest Dec (2.03), lowest Sep (1.97).
Challenging the results: multiple-testing, sample sizes, outliers, robustness…
⚠ 'product_revenue by payment_method' was significant on its own (p=0.0296) but not after correcting for 19 comparisons (adjusted p=0.562); treat it as a lead, not a result.
'product_revenue by payment_method' is statistically detectable but the effect is small (eta_squared=0.002), so it may not matter in practice; no action is recommended from it alone.
